title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཇེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 176)
shelf_note: A Pramāṇa commentary (on apoha and universals, sāmānya) in the Derge Tengyur tshad ma section. It belongs on this shelf.

ocr_errors.problem: ldog/log spelling variant (low confidence at this resolution)

ocr_errors.image: seems to read མཚན་ཉིད་ཅན་དུ་གྱུར་པའོ (the OCR's ཀྱིར is not a word)
ocr_errors.problem: garbled syllable; the sense is still recoverable

ocr_errors.image: the syllable is unclear: བརྟགས or བརྟན. The argument (a permanent universal cannot be benefited) expects 'permanent'
ocr_errors.problem: possible misreading of permanent as imputed; it splits the two translations

tr_errors_A.english: because conceptual thought arises through a process of excluding its own characteristic
tr_errors_A.problem: drops 'indirectly' (བརྒྱུད་པས), which is the point of the argument; the svalakṣaṇa's exclusion is turned into thought excluding its own characteristic

tr_errors_A.english: not something metaphorically ascribed. The phrase is applied
tr_errors_A.problem: loses the gloss that the word 'exists' (ཡོད་པ) is to be construed here

tr_errors_A.english: this clearly illustrates the point that these factors gradually become the cause of conceptual thought
tr_errors_A.problem: a quoted root-text phrase ('by those that gradually become causes…') is turned into a free-standing claim
the gloss 'samakara' is not a plausible Sanskrit equivalent; looks invented

tr_errors_A.english: since it is imputed and lacks any practical efficiency
tr_errors_A.problem: follows a doubtful OCR reading ('imputed'); 'lacks practical efficiency' misreads 'cannot be benefited'

tr_errors_A.english: This has already been explained, and it is applied here
tr_errors_A.problem: the lemma being connected is no longer marked as a quotation

tr_errors_B.english: is itself ultimately real, whereas nominal imputation does not exist in reality; in this manner the words are connected
tr_errors_B.problem: misparse: the source says this nature is ultimate, not imputed, and that 'exists' is to be construed with it. It does not say that imputation does not exist

tr_errors_B.english: an unchanging entity cannot produce any benefit
tr_errors_B.problem: has the direction backwards: the universal cannot be benefited (anupakārya), not 'cannot produce benefit'

pages.prefer_reason: Neither version has a serious error. B keeps the quoted lemmas and the key 'indirectly' (བརྒྱུད་པས) and reads the permanence argument plausibly; A has more moderate slips and an invented gloss.

book_verdict: This is the right leaf, and the woodblock text is transcribed well apart from a few doubtful syllables. Both translations are serviceable and have no serious errors; B is the more precise of the two.
